title: Similarity
outcome: By the end, I can calculate similarity under a declared feature rule and explain a changed ranking.
scenario: A fictional craft-card matcher compares each candidate with a target.
given: Target: red, round, smooth. A: red,square,smooth. B: blue,round,smooth. C: red,round,rough.
Initially each exact feature match scores 1; return all highest scorers.
For the second comparison only, colour and shape matches score 1 each and a texture match scores 3.

steps.label: Target features
steps.detail: Compare colour, shape and texture separately.

steps.label: Equal weights
steps.detail: A matches colour+texture=2; B shape+texture=2; C colour+shape=2.

steps.label: Texture weight 3
steps.detail: New scores A=4, B=4, C=2; A and B remain tied.

explanation: Similarity is defined by the chosen representation and weights. The cards did not change when texture gained weight; the comparison rule did. Two high scores need not mean two identical cards. A complete rule also says what to do with tied scores, rather than choosing whichever appears first by accident.

counterfactual.change: Keep original weights but change the target texture to rough.
counterfactual.prediction: C scores 3; A and B each score 1.
counterfactual.reason: C now matches all three target features; the others lose their smooth-texture match.

student_task: Point to the matches supporting C’s new score and explain why there is no tie.
teacher_answer: C matches red, round and rough: 3. A matches only red and B only round: 1 each.
project_evidence: Declare sorter similarity features, weights and tie behavior before using scores to explain recommendations.
limits: A high feature-match score does not establish usefulness or suitability beyond the features represented.
review_note: New fictional worked case reviewed against the weekly topic and reserved independent assessment. Keep that assessment separate; this picture is supported practice.
